column1: # dispatch-model-display.tsv -- DGN-1444: runtime model vocabulary and owner display.
# DATA, not logic. Shell dispatch and Python status-footer both read this file.
# One row owns the concrete runtime slug and owner-facing display for one
# (runtime, model) pair. Adding a future runtime model is one row here.
# Columns (TAB-separated): runtime  model  observed_slug  display
# observed_slug is the concrete runtime identifier persisted in status.json;
# display is presentation-only, the full model name "<Vendor> <Family> <version>"
# (owner 2026-09-27 13:38, DGN-1752; supersedes DGN-1227 dec-177's no-vendor form).
# Codex rows carry the full display (the slug pins the version). Claude rows
# carry the bare "Claude <Family>": the CLI decides the
# version at run time, so it is derived from the model id the run reports
# (lib/model_display.py); the bare name shows only until an id is observed.
# lib/model_display.py is the only reader/parser of this file.
# Optional 5th column: surfaces the row is offered on, comma-separated
# ("chat" = the bridge /model picker, DGN-1814 r3). model_table() reads the
# rows layered vendor -> family -> version (Claude / Opus / 5.5), so a second
# chat-selectable vendor is rows marked "chat" here -- the picker turns
# two-step (vendor, then family) by itself.
